newsitem.title: USA: Gore says room for U.S. wages to keep growing.
newsitem.headline: Gore says room for U.S. wages to keep growing.

text.p: Fresh reports showing slow rates of consumer price rises in an expanding economy prove that wages can grow safely without firing up inflation, Vice President Albert Gore said Friday.
"There is room in the economy for wages to go up without igniting inflation," Gore said at a White House ceremony to announce awarding of more than $800 million in grants to poor communities.
Gore said a government report on Friday showing consumer prices went up only a slight 0.1 percent in August was "the best possible news for the economy."
He said it shows that it is possible to create jobs, to have both stock and bond markets improve and yet to keep inflation well down.
Gore emphasized that wages have only recently begun to improve again and pointed out that there is no indication, as some have feared, that the gains pose an inflation risk.
"As wages have begun to go back up again, inflation has not," Gore said adding, "We think it can continue."
